summary: Cynthea J. Bogel is a scholar in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She completed her doctoral studies under John M. Rosenfield and held an attested post at the University of Washington between 2004 and 2009.
Cynthia Col works in sinology and religious studies. She studied Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003) and studied under Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman.

Cynthia M. Beall is a tibetologist. She earned a B.A. from the University of Pennsylvania (1966–1970) and an M.A. from Pennsylvania State University (1970–1976), and became a Distinguished University Professor and Professor of Anthropology at Case Western Reserve University in 1976.

Cynthia Talbot is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1980–1988) and became professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin around 2021.

Cyril Alexander Rylands was an Indologist and linguist who earned his B.A. and M.A. at the University of Cambridge. He served at SOAS University of London (attested 1949), where he was Lecturer in Sanskrit until 1961.

Cyril Henry Philips (1912–2005) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning degrees from the University of Liverpool and SOAS, he served as Director of SOAS (1946–1980) and Vice-Chancellor of the University of London (1972–1976).

Cyril Walter Gurner (1888–1960) was an Indology scholar who earned master's degrees from Oriel College (~1906–1910) and the University of London. He served as Treasurer of The Asiatic Society around 1944.

Cyrill von Korvin-Krasinski (1905–1992) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned a Ph.D. from Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1946–1948) and served as director of the abbey's school at Maria Laach Abbey.

Cyrus Ransom Pangborn (1916–1989) was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Kansas Wesleyan, Yale, and Columbia. He taught religion at the University of Iowa (1951–1954) and Rutgers University (1954–1982).

Cyrus Stearns is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Washington under Leonard van der Kuijp, also studying under Turrell V. Wylie and several Tibetan teachers. He worked as a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.
Cândido de Figueiredo (1846–1925) was an Indologist and linguist who studied law at the University of Coimbra (1869–1874). In 1882, he held a teaching post at Liceu Central.
Cécile Ducher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. under Matthew T. Kapstein at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where she also served as a research fellow.

Célestin Bouglé (1870–1940) was a scholar in philosophy and Indology who studied at the École Normale Supérieure. He held posts at Montpellier, Toulouse, the Sorbonne, the University of Paris, and served as Director of the École Normale Supérieure (1935–1940).

D. C. Lau (1921–2010) was a sinologist and philosopher educated at the University of Hong Kong and the University of Glasgow. He held professorships at the University of London and SOAS, and was Chair of Chinese at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (1978–1989).
D. C. Sarasvati was an Indologist who studied under V. Raghavan. She served as a Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras from 1964 to 1965.

D. Christian Lammerts is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. A former doctoral student at Cornell University (attested 2006), he served as Assistant Professor at Rutgers University (attested 2014–2020).

D. Dennis Hudson (1938–2006) specialized in religious studies and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from Claremont Graduate University (~1965–1970) and was a professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies at Smith College from 1970 to 2000.
D. G. Dhavale was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts as a professor at Fergusson College and Savitribai Phule Pune University.
D. H. Gordon (1895–1961) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He was educated at Wellington College (~1909–1913) and the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst (~1913–1914).

D. L. Narasimhachar (1906–1971) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1925–1929), and served on the faculty at the University of Mysore from around 1932 to 1962.
